updates.statement: Accuracy per step is set by the structure of the update. Only effects of about 0.6 pp or more are robust under the corrected noise model (~0.2 pp sd on a 3-seed mean, ~0.28 pp on an unpaired difference). These are: Muon on the conv filters (+1.3 pp, E014), lookahead (~0.9-1 pp, E008/E020), the Muon lr cliffs (0.36: E019; 0.12: E075), frequency-split orthogonalization (E030), whitening weaker than NS3 (E065) and a 1x1 final map (E050). Most other closures (E033, E036, E046, E049, E060, E066, E068, E072) and the force-keeps (E024, E026, E042, E045, E052) are single runs within ~1-2 sd. So 'the update geometry is saturated' is NOT established. The recipe may be a random walk over flat directions. The Polar Express gain (E069) is doubtful: its 13-seed mean is ~0.7534, and both the PE paper's own CIFAR runs and MUD's airbench table find no gain from stronger orthogonalization. Remaining directions should be screened offline on 10-20+ seeds in one process for TRUE-mean gain: averaging setup (H1.6.1), schedule shape (new), logit scale (new), the airbench96 residual check (new), and the width split (H1.12).

E053 (step-starving the low-res phase) and E055 (bs 2048 -0.45) suggest fewer steps hurt broadly. Under the current noise a ~2% time cut that changes the math is a gate lottery. Lowered.

E066 -0.26 against a +0.25 prediction is ~1.8 sd of an unpaired 3-seed difference under the corrected noise model. Unlikely to be a gain, but harm is not established. Downgraded from refuted per the review.

The seeds-0-2 +0.24 pp is not confirmed: 13-seed mean ~0.7534. The PE paper's own CIFAR runs and MUD's airbench table (Muon3 ~= Muon5) both find no gain from stronger orthogonalization. Awaiting the paired H1.2.9 computation from existing data.
Its rationale (PE moved the lr optimum) is weakened by search showing PE gives no CIFAR gain. Do not run it before H1.2.9 is computed.

Search lowers the prior that PE beats NS3 by >=0.1 pp. This costs nothing to compute from existing seeds-3-12 runs and should be done before any PE-dependent run. Report the paired per-seed sd and SE alongside the delta.

updates.statement: On the current base (E081 code, deterministic kernels if H2.5.1 holds), after the H1.6.6 check, a stronger or denser averaging setup gives >=+0.15 pp in TRUE mean at <=1% more time. Screen offline in ONE process on >=20 seeds, and launch only a candidate whose paired gain is >=2 SE. Candidates in priority order: (t/T)^2 instead of (t/T)^3 ramp; lookahead sync every 3 steps instead of 5; a late-started EMA on top of lookahead, initialized from the current weights (hlb-CIFAR10 starts its EMA for the last ~80% with a cubic ramp).
updates.reason: Review: averaging is the second-largest measured lever, yet it has had only one tuning run (E028, decay only). Search: hlb-CIFAR10's late-started EMA and LAWA give weak prior art. Statement updated with the base and a proper offline gate.
E033 -0.17 against a +0.2 prediction is ~1.3 sd under the corrected noise model, a single run. Downgraded from refuted. The tail-floor axis is flat or slightly negative, not closed.
Still open and offline/cheap. It should run before H1.6.1. E028's 0.003 pp match with its parent remains the suspicious case. The Dynamo float-guard argument lowers the prior a little.

updates.statement: The SGD-group lrs are flat within about +-0.3 pp around head x2 / BN-bias x64. Only the clearly worse sides are established: head x0.5 (-0.41, E039) and BN x128 (-0.49, E056), each a single run of ~1.5-2 sd. Head x2 (E045 +0.18), x3 (E049 -0.03) and BN x32 (E072 -0.13 vs the lucky tip, ~+0.14 vs E069's 13-seed mean) are all within noise, so the optimum is unresolved. This still rests on the multipliers actually being applied in the compiled path (H1.6.6).
updates.reason: Review: the 'at optimum' claim rested on noise-sized single runs. Status changed to inconclusive.
E036 -0.02 against a +0.2 prediction is ~0.8 sd. With E004 it suggests LS is flat, but this is not a refutation at the corrected noise level.
E072 -0.13 vs the lucky tip is ~+0.14 vs E069's 13-seed mean, well within noise of the +0.2 prediction. Downgraded from refuted.
E068 -0.24 against a +0.25 prediction is ~1.8 sd on an unpaired difference vs E058, whose own true mean is unknown. A gain is unlikely, but this is a single run. Downgraded per the review.

updates.statement: With the recipe held fixed, per-trial GPU work can still be cut by a few percent, but only by removing GPU work: launch overhead is hidden (E005, E038). Math-preserving cuts found so far: E078 fused per-epoch augment (-2.5%), E077 build-time prepare warmups (-1.3%), and E081 bundling both (-3.7%). All three failed the gate on process-level re-draws, not on their effect. They become gate-neutral only if kernel selection is made deterministic across processes (H2.5.1); otherwise every 'math-preserving' cut is a ~50% lottery at E069's true mean of ~0.7534. Earlier systems total: ~11% (E007, E010, E021, E023, E034), plus the curriculum (H2.3) and the block-1 freeze (E058 -4.7%). Smaller levers left: Gram NS (<=~1% end to end, math-changing), projection frequency (H2.4.3, math-changing), and remaining outside-step overhead (new H3 child).
updates.reason: E077/E078/E081 support the time claim. The review shows these cuts are blocked by build-perturbation nondeterminism, so determinism is now a prerequisite.

updates.statement: Applying the Muon weight-norm projection only every 2+int(15*progress) steps (Hiverge's exact rule) instead of every step cuts mean time by >=1.5% with true-mean accuracy within +-0.15 pp. Caveat (search): Hiverge pairs intermittent projection with Muon weight decay, which the tip lacks, so weight norms may drift between projections. This change alters the math, so judge it on an offline same-process screen of >=20 seeds, not on seeds 0-2.
updates.reason: Search gives the exact Hiverge rule and the weight-decay confound. Prior lowered slightly.
MUD and the PE paper show no CIFAR benefit from orthogonalization accuracy, and E065 shows a cliff below NS3. NS2 has <1% upside and a real risk of falling below the cliff. Not worth a run.

Search confirms the FLOP arithmetic (60 vs 84 n^3) and the stability recipe (restart after iteration 2, safety factor 1.05). Its measured speedups are only on large LM matrices, and with Muon at ~6% of the run the end-to-end ceiling is ~1%. It changes rounding, so it falls into the gate lottery unless bundled. Lowered.

updates.statement: Conv algorithm selection and conv shapes are not where time goes. Odd spatial sizes cost almost nothing (E032), and max-autotune/cudnn.benchmark gained ~1.1% at most (E007, within jitter). Their real cost is nondeterminism: timing-based kernel choice differs whenever build() state changes, which turns every edit into a full per-seed re-draw (E077). They also add a 77 s build and kernel choices tuned on the SXM that may not transfer to the PCIe judge.
updates.reason: Reframed as a determinism question per the review and the PyTorch-docs finding on Inductor autotuning.

updates.statement: Determinism test. Build E081 with cudnn.benchmark=False and torch.compile without max-autotune. Also check whether Inductor's Triton pointwise/reduction autotuning in torch 2.4 can change reduction order, and pin or disable any such config benchmarking. Prediction: per-seed accuracies on seeds 0-2 reproduce bit-identically across two processes whose build() warmups differ, and mean time stays within +1.5% of autotuned E081. If so, later math-preserving cuts inherit their base's gate outcome. Launch once and accept the single harness draw; no re-rolls. Refuted if any seed differs by >0.02 pp across the two processes, or time rises >2%.
updates.reason: Review: this is the structural fix for the loop's main blocker (four real time cuts parked behind the gate lottery). Search: the PyTorch docs name Inductor on-device benchmarking as a source of numeric differences.

updates.statement: Fixed and per-epoch overheads outside the train step are a few percent of the score, not >10%: ~4% at a ~4.6 s run (E077 prepare first-use -1.3%; E078 per-epoch augment/permute/gather -2.5%, from 0.16 to ~0.06 s/trial). Their share grows as step time shrinks: E003 measured ~2% at 8.3 s. They can be cut bit-identically by moving warmups into build() and writing only consumed samples.
updates.reason: Reworded per the review. The original >10% claim is false, but E077/E078 found ~4% of real overhead that E003 had dismissed at 2%.

updates.statement: The binding constraint is the LOCAL accuracy gate (3-seed mean on fixed seeds 0-2 >= 0.753), not the official one. E069's true (13-seed) mean is ~0.7534, so any edit, including math-preserving ones, passes with probability ~50-55%: every edit changes build() state, which changes the autotuned kernels and re-draws all seeds (E077). The 3-seed mean sd is ~0.2 pp. E070-E081 all missed, including four real time cuts (E077, E078, E080, E081). Per Jordan (2304.01910), seed variance is mostly test-set sampling noise, so no recipe change can shrink it. The only ways through are: (a) a higher true mean, about >=0.7555 for >=85% pass probability (H4.5); or (b) deterministic kernel selection, so math-preserving cuts inherit the base's draw (H2.5.1). Score candidates against 13-20+ seed means, never against seeds 0-2 deltas below ~0.3 pp.
updates.reason: Updated with the E077 noise mechanism and the search finding that variance is test-set noise. Escape routes added.

updates.statement: Noise on the local gate is dominated by build-perturbation nondeterminism. An unchanged commit reruns bit-identically (E003; I102 on E069). But any edit that changes build() state (warmups, graph set, allocator) shifts cudnn.benchmark/max-autotune kernel choices, and the ~220-step chaotic run turns the different rounding into a full per-seed re-draw. E077, math-identical and verified bit-identical offline, moved seeds by -0.25/+0.14/-0.84 pp. The effective sd for ANY code change is ~0.2 pp on the 3-seed mean and ~0.35-0.4 pp per seed (Jordan's sqrt(err(1-err)/n) gives the same order). E057's 0.06 pp was one draw and understates it.
updates.reason: Rewritten per the review around E077's mechanism. Supported by E077 together with the I102 bit-identical reruns.

E077-: true only for bit-identical commits. For post-E007 configs any edit to build() re-draws per-seed accuracy by up to 0.84 pp, so 'reruns spread <=0.15 pp' does not describe the noise on a comparison.
E077-: a math-neutral edit moved the 3-seed mean by 0.32 pp (one seed by 0.84), far above the <=0.08 pp predicted. E057's small shift was a single favourable draw.
Superseded by the H4.1 rewrite: any build change re-draws, so RNG-shift edits add little. The regression-to-the-mean question is answered by E069's 13-seed mean (~0.7534 vs 0.7561).

I102 reported unchanged E069 reruns as bit-identical on seeds 0-2, and E077 shows edited builds re-draw. Together these confirm that kernel autotuning, not process-level randomness in unchanged builds, is the noise source. The PyTorch docs (search) describe the mechanism.

updates.statement: Official safety is not the risk. On 13 seeds E069's mean (~0.7534) sits ~0.34 pp above the official 40-seed bar of 0.75. Per Jordan, seed spread is mostly test-set noise, so the 40-seed mean is stable. With a per-run sd of ~0.35 pp the 40-seed mean has sd ~0.06 pp. The PCIe judge will autotune different kernels, which is one more unbiased draw. Pending: restate the headroom using the EMPIRICAL per-seed sd of E069's 13 existing seeds. A recipe whose 13-seed mean stays >=0.752 is officially safe even if it misses the local gate.
updates.reason: Review asks for an empirical sd and notes the judge's kernel draw. Search supports the stability claim.
E070-E081 all missed against the lucky 0.7561, including math-identical cuts (E077, E078, E081) whose true mean equals E069's. Regression to the mean is confirmed.
Rescored against 0.7534: E072 +0.14, E071 +0.17, E076 -0.27, E073 -0.11 and E074 -0.21 are all within +-0.3 pp. E075 -0.62 and E070 -0.36 stay beyond it. This matches the prediction exactly.

updates.statement: Time is set by full-resolution compute after warmup. Warmup steps tolerate low resolution (E040, E047, E048; 18 px in E080) but not fewer steps (E053). Low-res steps after the lr peak cost ~0.2 pp per half-epoch moved from 32 to 28 px (E043, E054, E074 vs the 13-seed mean). The final map must stay >=2x2 (E050, E080). The epoch slope at the knee is uncertain by ~3x. Against E069's 13-seed mean, E070 is ~-0.36 pp for -0.25 epoch (~1.4 pp/epoch). E063's +0.07 for +0.25 epoch is a single run on another base. It must be measured directly offline (H4.5 child) before E081's savings are spent on epochs.
updates.reason: Review: the slope was built from a lucky baseline and a single cross-base run. Rescored E070; confidence lowered.

Both explanations now have data. Training the bias longer gave no gain (E060). An 18 px stage with a 2x2 final map costs nothing (E080, offline paired +0.03 pp on seeds 3-12), while 16 px with a 1x1 map collapsed (E050). The structural threshold explains the cliff.
E080+: the offline paired delta was +0.03 pp on seeds 3-12, well within -0.25 pp. The seeds-0-2 miss is the expected gate lottery. The notebook verdict supports this.

Unchanged prior. Run it only as an offline same-process screen on >=20 seeds, gated at 2 SE, after the airbench96 residual check (new node), since a missing residual would change the block-1/2 capacity picture.

new.statement: Gate escape through true-mean margin. A recipe whose true (13-20+ seed) mean is >=~0.7555 passes the 3-seed gate with probability >=85% (sd ~0.2 pp). Reaching it lets the parked math-preserving cuts (E078, E077, E081) be stacked. The cheapest route is to spend part of E081's -3.7% on epochs or the averaging setup, and rank all candidates by offline true-mean gain per % time, not by seeds-0-2 deltas.

Offline in one process on seeds 3-22, compare E081 at 6.75 epochs with E081 at 7.0 epochs (extra 0.25 epoch in the 32 px stage, freeze kept at 0.8 of samples, all schedules sample-indexed). Prediction: +0.25 epoch raises the true mean by >=+0.2 pp (paired, >=2 SE), at time <= E069's 4.68 s (expected ~4.65 s: E081 4.51 s + ~3.5%). If the gain is <0.1 pp, the knee is flat above 6.75 and epochs cannot buy margin.

Conditional on N1a. E081 at 7.0 epochs (built deterministically if H2.5.1 holds) launched once on seeds 0-2 clears 0.753 at time < 4.678 s (E069), giving the first new feasible tip since E069. Its 20-seed offline mean will be >=0.7550.

Pairing on seed buys little for any math-changing edit. From existing offline data (E079 and E080 on seeds 3-12 vs E069), the paired per-seed sd of the delta will be >=0.25 pp, close to the unpaired ~0.35-0.4 pp, because chaotic training re-draws per-example test errors regardless of shared data order. Consequence: a 10-seed offline delta has SE ~0.1 pp, so the E079/E080 gates set at 0.05 pp could not resolve their own thresholds. Gates must be >=2 SE, or use 20-40 seeds with both arms in one process. Refuted if the paired sd is <=0.12 pp.

The logit scale (temperature) inherited from airbench96 (logits x 1/9) was tuned for 10 classes. With 100 classes it sets the softmax sharpness, the gradient sent back to the features, and the effective head lr (head x2 helped, x3 ~= x2). It may be mis-set for this task.

First check in drafts/ whether the port applies a fixed logit scale. If it does, screen scales of 1/6 and 1/12 offline in one process on >=20 seeds against E081, with LS 0.2 and the head lr unchanged. Prediction: one of them gives >=+0.15 pp true-mean gain (paired, >=2 SE) at zero time cost. If both are within +-1 SE, the axis is flat.

airbench96's depth-3 ConvGroup has a residual (x = conv3(...) + x0). Check in drafts/ whether the arena port kept it. If it was dropped, restoring it in every block gives >=+0.2 pp true-mean gain (offline, >=20 seeds, >=2 SE) at <1% time. A restored residual would also invalidate the skip-free assumptions behind the freeze results (E062, H7). If the port already has it, retire this node as not applicable.

The global lr schedule shape (23% warmup from 0.2x, linear decay to a 0.07x floor) was inherited from SGD airbench and never varied as a whole on the Muon+curriculum base. Only the Muon-only warmup (E031) and a bundled SGD change (E012) were tried. Because the tail and averaging interact strongly (E025 -0.51), the shape may be off its optimum by more than the single-knob tests could see.

Offline in one process on >=20 seeds against E081, with the 0.07x floor and the low-res stage boundaries kept and both groups changed together: (a) warmup 0.23 -> 0.15; (b) warmup 0.23 -> 0.30, so the 20 px stage sits fully inside warmup. Prediction: one of them gives a true-mean gain of >=+0.15 pp (paired, >=2 SE) at unchanged time. If both are within 1 SE, the schedule axis is flat.

Outside-step work that the per-step profiles never covered still costs a visible share of the trial: the split straddling steps at the 50k/75k/175k/270k-sample switches, lookahead syncs, the final partial epoch, and the end-of-train copy and eval prep. Re-profile the whole trial after every ~10% cut in total time.

A full-trial profile of E081 will show >=0.05 s per trial (>=1%) in straddling-step splits, lookahead syncs and other non-train-step work that can be removed bit-identically, for example by fusing the lookahead blend into the Muon step or merging the straddling partial steps into precompiled shapes. Report E078's profile items (b)-(d), which were gathered but never recorded. If they total <0.03 s, the outside-step axis is closed.

structured_output.summary:
The review's noise model is adopted. Any edit to build() changes which kernels autotuning picks, and that re-draws every seed (E077): about 0.2 pp sd on the 3-seed mean, about 0.35-0.4 pp per seed. Under this model:
- H4.1 is rewritten and marked supported.
- H4.1.1 and H4.1.4 are refuted, H4.1.7 is supported, and H4.1.6 is retired.
- H4.4 and H4.4.1 are supported. Rescored against E069's 13-seed mean (~0.7534), every result lands where H4.4.1 predicted.
- Six closures that were single runs within ~1-2 sd move from refuted to inconclusive: H1.2.6, H1.6.4, H1.7.2, H1.7.4 and H1.11.1, plus H1.7 as a whole.
- H1 no longer claims the update geometry is saturated. Only effects of about 0.6 pp or more count as robust.

Search shows no CIFAR gain from stronger orthogonalization: the Polar Express paper's own CIFAR runs, and MUD's airbench table (Muon3 ≈ Muon5). This lowers H1.2.7, H1.2.8 and H1.2.9, and H2.4.6 is retired. Gram NS (H2.4.8) is capped at about 1% end to end.

H2.5.1 is reframed as a determinism test: build without cudnn.benchmark and max-autotune so that math-preserving cuts give bit-identical seeds. H2 now counts the time cuts blocked only by the gate (E078 -2.5%, E077 -1.3%, E081 bundle -3.7%). H3 is reworded: overhead outside the train step is about 4% and grows in share as steps get faster. H6.1 and H6.1.2 are supported (the 18 px stage keeps a 2x2 map and is fine). H6's epoch slope is marked uncertain by about 3x.

New nodes:
- **H4 escape route (N1).** Raise the true mean to about 0.7555 or more, mainly by spending E081's savings on epochs. N1a measures the epoch slope offline; N1b is the conditional launch.
- **Noise check (N2).** Pairing on seed buys little for math-changing edits, so offline gates need at least 2 SE.
- **Untried directions.** Logit scale (N3/N3a), whether the port kept the airbench96 residual (N4), and global schedule shape (N5/N5a).
- **Outside-step overhead (N6/N6a).** A full-trial re-profile.

H1, H2 and H4 remain open at Lvl1.
